key_findings: 27 cadaveric arms (24 paired, 3 unpaired). Coracobrachialis was "two-headed muscle in 62.96% (17/27 arms), a three-headed in 22.2% (6/27), a one-headed in 11.1% (3/27), and a four-headed in 3.7% (1 arm)"; MCN coursed between CB superficial and deep heads in 100% (24/24) of multi-headed CB. Interconnections: lateral cord-medial root of MN 18.52%, "musculocutaneous with the median nerve in 7.41%", radial-ulnar 3.71%; lateral root of MN duplicated in 11.1%.
clinical_relevance: "Careful dissection and knowledge of relatively common variants play a significant role in reducing iatrogenic injury."
notes: Doubles as topo_variation (CB morphology, MCN-MN interconnection). Same author group (Piagkou) as PMC12619963.

topic: Coracobrachialis morphology types and musculocutaneous nerve formation/innervation patterns (100 limbs)

figures.label: Fig. 1
figures.caption: The morphological types of the CBM. (A) Single belly CBM (type I) originating from the CP of scapula in common with the SH with superficial course of MCN. (B) Two-headed CBM (type II) shows superficial head (1) originating from CP and deep head (2) originating from SH with passage of MCN between them. (C) The three-headed CBM (type III) exhibits two superficial heads (1, 2) originating from the SH directly or through a common tendon and a deep head (3) originating from CP and inserts into the middle of anteromedial surface of humerus with passage of MCN between its superficial and deep heads. The 4th head (4) fuses with the common tendon of biceps brachii muscle. key_findings: 120 formalin-fixed upper limbs. key_findings: 107 healthy adults (mean age 46). Radial nerve CSA (mm2): above SG 7.02 ± 1.87, SG 6.81 ± 1.75, antecubital fossa 7.26 ± 1.70; median nerve mid-arm 9.34 ± 2.38; ulnar mid-arm 6.37 ± 1.56; MACN mid-arm 3.30 ± 1.13; MC axilla 3.81 ± 1.28 (Table 1). topic: Supracondylar process of the humerus on X-ray, CT and US
title: Imaging of elbow entrapment neuropathies
authors: Albano Domenico, Di Rocco Gabriella, Gitto Salvatore et al.

figures.label: Fig. 8
figures.caption: X-ray (a), CT (b), and US (c) of the supracondylar process (arrow)
figures.what_it_shows: Supracondylar process (arrow) on oblique radiograph of the distal humerus (a), axial CT through the distal arm (b) and ultrasound (c).
figures.labels_visible_in_image: a., b., c., white arrows

key_findings: Narrative review: "A supracondylar process is a bony spur arising from the anteromedial humerus, approximately 3-6 cm proximal to the medial epicondyle, and is present in 1-2% of individuals." It "can be easily detected on X-ray images obtained in oblique views but may not be identified in anteroposterior or lateral views alone." On US it "appears as a thick echogenic line with distal acoustic shadowing, while the Struthers' ligament appears as a thin, hypoechoic linear structure."
clinical_relevance: "Supracondylar process syndrome refers to the compression of the MN under this bony process or ligament."
notes: Figure is small (790x212 composite) but the spur is clear. Prevalence is cited, not original.

key_findings: 500 upper limbs of 250 volunteers. "15.6% of the participants in our study had the accessory brachial artery anatomical variation" (39 participants: bilateral 6 = 2.4%, right only 20 = 8%, left only 13 = 5.2%); no sex difference (p = 0.401).
